title_ar: الشيخ الددو يُلقي سلسلة محاضرات بانواذيبو عن: "سنة التمكين" و"دور العمل الخيري"
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Delivers a Series of Lectures in Nouadhibou on "God's Established Way of Empowerment" and "The Role of Charitable Work"
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء سلسلة محاضرات في مدينة انواذيبو يوم السبت 25 فبراير 2012 ، الموافق: 03 ربيع الثاني 1433 هـ . وقد ألقيت المحاضرة الأولى في مسجد قُبَاء، تحت عنوان: "والعاقبة للمتقين"، وذلك بعد صلاة العصر، كما ألقيت المحاضرة الثانية بمسجد "كانصادو"، تناولت موضوع: "العمل الخيري ودوره في خدمة الدعوة"، وقد خُصص جزء من هذه المحاضرة لطرح استفتاءات المحاضرين والرد عليها من الشيخ. تناولت المحاضرة الأولى للشيخ، العناصر التالية: • التنبيه إلى حكم رفع الصوت بالمساجد ونحوه دون سبب شرعي، وآداب طلب العلم، والصدع بالحق. • من سنن الله في الكون الصراع الأبدي بين الحق والباطل • أركان الطغيان الخمسة: 1- الملك الجبار. 2- والوزير المنافق المتملق. 3- ورجل المال والأعمال الذي يُسخِّر ماله لاستتباب الظلم والتمكين له. 4- رجل الدين الذي يسوغ الظلم ويبرر للفساد ويدافع عن الاستبداد. 5- رجل الإعلام الذي يطمس الحقيقة، ويروج الأباطيل. • وعند اجتماع هذه الأركان الخمسة تأتي سنة الله "والعاقبة للمتقين". بعد الفوز في الامتحان والابتلاء الذي يصيب المؤمنين من سطوة المُلك الجبار والحكم الظالم. • شروط تحقق سنة الله بغلبة الحق. • عودة سنن الله مرة بعد أخرى، كما هو الحال في الثورات التي قامت في بعض البلدان العربية الإسلامية. كما تناولت المحاضرة الثانية موضوع العمل الخيري، ودوره في خدمة الدعوة والرقي بالمجتمع، والردود على أسئلة واستفتاءات الحاضرين. وقد حضر هذا النشاط الدعوي جمهور غفير من شباب مدينة انواذيبو وشخصيات كبيرة؛ رجال أعمال ومسؤولين، إلى جانب الحضور المميز لكل الأعمار رجالا ونساء من جميع شرائح المجتمع.
body_en:
The eminent scholar Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a series of lectures in the city of Nouadhibou on Saturday 25 February 2012, corresponding to 3 Rabi' al-Thani 1433 AH.

The first lecture was delivered at the Quba Mosque, under the title "And the final outcome belongs to the God-conscious", after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr). The second lecture was delivered at the "Cansado" Mosque and took up the subject "Charitable Work and Its Role in Serving the Call to Islam (daʿwah)"; part of this lecture was set aside for the putting of requests for legal opinions by those present and for the Sheikh's answers to them.

The Sheikh's first lecture took up the following elements:

- Drawing attention to the ruling on raising the voice in mosques and the like without a reason recognised in the Sharia; the proprieties of seeking knowledge; and speaking out plainly with the truth.
- Among God's established ways in the cosmos is the perpetual struggle between truth and falsehood.
- The five pillars of tyranny: 1. The despotic king. 2. The hypocritical, fawning minister. 3. The man of money and business who harnesses his wealth to make injustice settled and firmly established. 4. The man of religion who makes injustice seem permissible, provides justifications for corruption, and defends despotism. 5. The man of media who blots out the truth and promotes falsehoods.
- And when these five pillars come together, God's established way arrives: "and the final outcome belongs to the God-conscious" — after success in the testing and the trial that befalls the believers from the might of despotic kingship and unjust rule.
- The conditions for the realisation of God's established way in the victory of the truth.
- The recurrence of God's established ways time after time, as is the case in the revolutions that have taken place in some Arab Muslim countries.

The second lecture likewise took up the subject of charitable work and its role in serving the call to Islam and in raising society up, and the answers to the questions and the requests for legal opinions from those present.

This missionary activity was attended by a vast public of the young people of the city of Nouadhibou and by prominent figures — businessmen and officials — alongside a notable attendance of every age, men and women, from all strata of society.

flags.arabic: أركان الطغيان الخمسة ... رجل الدين الذي يسوغ الظلم ويبرر للفساد ويدافع عن الاستبداد
flags.context: the five-part analysis of tyranny, summarised by the news desk as a list of headings
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. The list is a direct political indictment — of rulers, ministers, financiers, religious scholars who serve power, and the press — and the final item explicitly reads the Arab revolutions of 2011 as an instance of God's established way. Read in English out of its 2012 Mauritanian context, and with the Sheikh's name on it, this carries real reputational and in some jurisdictions legal weight. Nothing has been softened and nothing strengthened. But the words are the news desk's compressed headings, not a transcript, and the corpus has no recording behind them; whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: التنبيه إلى حكم رفع الصوت بالمساجد ونحوه دون سبب شرعي
flags.context: the first heading of the first lecture
options: render as the source does, with the ruling named and not stated
supply the ruling from the Maliki school
flags.note: Style guide section 10 in miniature. The heading says the Sheikh gave a ruling (ḥukm) on raising the voice in mosques and does not say what the ruling was. A reader will assume a prohibition; the record supports no such inference, and none of the five rulings may be supplied. 'A reason recognised in the Sharia' renders سبب شرعي without importing a ruling word.

flags.context: the heading of the five-part list
flags.note: HOMONYM WARNING. The glossary carries ركن (rukn) as 'essential element', a fiqh term whose omission invalidates an act. That sense is not in play here: أركان is used in its ordinary sense of the supports or constituents of a thing. The glossary rendering has deliberately not been used, since 'the essential elements of tyranny' would read as a technical legal classification.

flags.context: the news headline, against the lecture titles given in the body
options: render the headline term as 'God's established way of empowerment'
treat it as the actual title of the first lecture
flags.note: The headline advertises a lecture on 'sunnat al-tamkīn', but the body gives the first lecture's title as 'And the final outcome belongs to the God-conscious' and names no lecture by the headline's title. tamkīn is the establishment of the believers in the land, a Qur'anic theme; the headline appears to be the news desk's gloss of the lecture's theme rather than its title. Headline and body have both been rendered as they stand; the discrepancy is flagged, not resolved.

flags.context: وقد خُصص جزء من هذه المحاضرة لطرح استفتاءات المحاضرين والرد عليها من الشيخ
options: read as الحاضرين — 'those present', as the closing sentence of the same record has it
flags.note: Probable source typo. There was one lecturer, and the parallel sentence later in the record says 'the questions and requests for legal opinions from those present' (الحاضرين). Preserved in body_ar, rendered on the reading the record itself supplies, flagged rather than fixed.

flags.context: the title of the first lecture, quoted twice
options: And the final outcome belongs to the God-conscious (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:128)
And the outcome is for the pious
And the end belongs to those who fear God
flags.note: A Qur'anic phrase used as a lecture title, given by the source in ordinary quotation marks and with no reference. The English keeps the quotation marks rather than the curly-brace convention of style guide section 4, since it is functioning as a title; the reference is Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:128. المتقين is rendered from the glossary's taqwā, 'God-consciousness'. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive.

translator_notes: A news-desk report giving the skeleton of two lectures as a list of headings. It is not a transcript, and the corpus has no text of either lecture.
The CMS timestamp, 27 February 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the lectures to Saturday 25 February 2012.
'سنن الله' is rendered 'God's established ways' throughout and is NOT the glossary's سنن ('the sunnah acts', worship). See the same warning on record 783.
انواذيبو and كانصادو are Nouadhibou and Cansado, the Mauritanian port city and its adjoining district; the French-derived spellings are standard in English.
